Paramecium, on the other hand, are single-celled organisms. They have a lot of organelles too, especially their contractile vacuoles which help them move. 

Looking at the options: 

A) They both move at the same rate. I'm not sure about this. I think Volvox might move in a group, so maybe some are faster than others, while Paramecium might move individually at their own rate. So maybe their rates aren't the same.

B) They both move away from light. I remember that many organisms, including Volvox, tend to move away from light to avoid being seen by predators. Paramecium might also do this. So this could be a similarity.

C) They both move in the same direction. I think Volvox tends to move in a particular direction, maybe towards food or away from light, but Paramecium might move in random directions because they're single cells and not coordinated. So maybe they don't both move in the same direction.

D) They both move toward an energy source. I'm not sure if they both specifically move towards energy. Volvox might move towards nutrients, but Paramecium might just move randomly as they don't have a directed response to energy sources like that.

So, considering all this, the most likely answer is B) They both move away from light because both organisms would want to avoid being exposed, and moving away from light is a common strategy for both.
